text:
**My pick: JBL Charge 6 (about $130-$150).** It's the top pick at What Hi-Fi and Best Products. It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and can charge your phone. Best Products praises its loud, bassy sound and tough build. [What Hi-Fi review and prices](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) · [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Other good options by need**

- **Loudest, for pool parties:** JBL Boombox 4. RTINGS rates it the best waterproof speaker it has tested. It floats, can be immersed for long periods, and lasts over 40 hours. It's big and sounds muffled if you're beside or behind it. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **360° sound around the pool:** Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM. It's IP67, floats, and gets about 15 hours. Tom's Guide ranks it best overall, and RTINGS calls it the best mid-range pick. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)
- **Budget:** Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4, about $65 on sale. It's IP67, floats, and gets 14 hours. [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- **Cheapest and tiny:** JBL Go 5, about $40. It's IP67 with up to 8 hours of battery, so it's quieter. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)
- **Easy to pack for the beach:** JBL Grip, $100. Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's IP68, under a pound, and about the size of a soda can, with 12 hours of battery. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **Big, bass-heavy floater:** Soundcore Boom 2 Plus. It's IPX7, floats, gets up to 20 hours, and weighs 3.8 kg. It lists at $249.99, and the code AFSC20 takes it to about $200. [Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus) (affiliate link, and the store's checkout has the final word on the price). The smaller Soundcore Boom 2 is about $110 and floats, but has no dust rating, so keep it on a towel at the beach.

**Tips**

- **Rating:** Aim for IP67 or IP68. Ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage, so rinse the speaker with fresh water afterward if the manual allows it, and dry it before charging. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **Ports:** Close the charging-port flap before it gets wet.
- **Sand:** Keep the speaker off the sand. Fine grit can get into openings.

Prices come from the review pages and change often, so check the current price before you buy.
